newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian politician resigns, names wife as successor.
newsitem.headline: Indian politician resigns, names wife as successor.

text.p: The scandal-tainted chief minister of India's eastern state of Bihar said on Friday he was resigning from his post, but immediately named his wife as his successor.

Laloo Prasad Yadav resigned less than an hour after India's Supreme Court ordered that he could not be arrested despite arrest warrants issued against him and three other politicians by a special investigative court in the Bihar state capital of Patna.
The United News of India (UNI) news agency said Yadav's wife Rabri Devi had been elected as his successor by his Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) party.

India has been fixated for weeks on the fate of the charismatic Yadav, who stubbornly refused for weeks to step down despite his indictment in a $280 million scandal involving the siphoning off of state agricultural funds.
The crisis has sharply divided the country's ruling United Front coalition, whose leaders put off until Friday evening a meeting on whether or not to allow Yadav's RJD group to remain in its fold.

Parliament has been rocked since its monsoon session started on Wednesday by bitter exchanges over Yadav. Friday's developments shook up the Bombay Stock Exchange, which fell sharply but then recovered some ground to end a provisional 38.83 points or 0.92 percent down at 4187.74.
